key_insight: External strain can strongly tune electron and hole g-factors in bulk CsPbX3, even driving them through zero, while nanocrystals are much less strain-sensitive because of quantum confinement.
engineering_relevance: This suggests strain engineering can be used to control spin-related properties in lead-halide perovskite devices, especially in bulk or weakly confined structures.
method: Parameters fitted to DFT target band structures
Linear-response calculation of g-factors under external strain; real-space calculations for nanocrystals
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical band-structure fitting and computed strain-dependent g-factors for both bulk and nanocrystal forms, showing a wide tunability range in bulk.
watch_item: The results are theoretical and focused on the reference cubic phase, so real-device behavior may differ due to defects, phase changes, and nonideal strain states.
paper_title: Strain tunability of electron and hole g-factors in CsPb$X_3$: bulk and nanocrystals
